To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a series of carboxylate phosphonate hybrid materials have been synthesized and structurally characterized.

(a) a series of carboxylate-phosphonates with manganese, aluminium and chromium cations has been prepared, (b) the crystal structures of the two solids containing manganese have been determined by the Rietvelt method, (c) the crystal structure of the aluminium compound has been solved from synchroton X-ray powder diffractions data, (d) the chromium compound has been characterized as an amorphous solid by IR-UV-VIs spectroscopy, and
a series of carboxylate-phosphonate hybrid solids have been prepared and characterized by a variety of methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis and characterization of a series of carboxylate phosphonates with a general formula of M(O3PCH 2CH2COO)(H2O) n (M = Mn(II) (1), Mn (III) (2), Al(III) (3) and (Cr(III) (4)) which are obtained by a hydrothermal method.

the synthesis and characterisation of a series of hybrid materials based on metal cations and organic phosphonate and/or carboxylate ligands, with the goal of developing materials with novel properties.
the synthesis of new metal carboxyphosphonates and their characterisation by X-ray and neutron diffraction, thermal and magnetic analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the synthesis and characterization of these compounds are a good example of the potential of X-ray diffraction and spectroscopic techniques in the characterization of hybrid materials, especially when they are not crystalline.
the phosphonate group is a good ligand for the synthesis of hybrid materials.
the carboxyethyl phosphonate ligand can be used to prepare a series of metal carboxyphosphonate solids with different inorganic layers, pillared or layered, and with different metal cations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have prepared and characterized a series of carboxylate-phosphonate hybrid inorganic-organic materials.

these compounds are the result of a combination of the structural features of the parent inorganic solids and those of the organic acid used as a building block, and the final structures are determined by the relative strength of the different interactions.

the carboxyethyl phosphonate ligand can act as a bidentate ligand to give rise to layered compounds (1 and 2) or as a tridentate ligand (3) to give rise to a pillared structure, or as an anion to give rise to amorphous compounds (4).
The main takeaway from our work is that
carboxyethyl phosphonic acid (CEPA) is able to form inorganic layers with Mn(II) cations and inorganic pillared structures with Al3(III) cation.
the synthesis of these compounds is not straightforward and the conditions used for their preparation are critical to their final structure and properties.
the carboxyethyl phosphonate ligand can be used as a building block for a variety of inorganic-organic hybrid materials.
